root_cause.text: The page fault handler in `xe_pagefault_service` failed to check whether the VMA is read-only before servicing write or atomic access requests, allowing unauthorized modifications to read-only VMAs.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds a check after VMA lookup: `if (xe_vma_read_only(vma) && pf->consumer.access_type != XE_PAGEFAULT_ACCESS_TYPE_READ)` returns `-EPERM`. The commit message explicitly states the handler should reject write/atomic access to read-only VMAs, and the fix references commit `fb544b844508` which originally implemented the page fault workqueue.

intent_record.intent_summary: Added a guard to reject non-read page faults on read-only VMAs, fixing a potential permission bypass.
intent_record.what: Added a conditional block after VMA lookup that checks if the VMA is read-only and the page fault access type is not a read; if so, sets err to -EPERM and jumps to unlock_vm.
intent_record.how: This change prevents servicing page faults that attempt non-read access (e.g., writes) on read-only VMAs, returning a permission error instead of proceeding with fault handling.

relevance_review.reason: The group adds a guard that checks VMA read-only status before servicing non-read page faults, directly fixing the missing permission check described in the vulnerability root cause.

candidates.rationale: This line computes the atomicity of the access but is executed without a prior check that the VMA is read-only. A write or atomic access to a read-only VMA would be incorrectly serviced, leading to a permission bypass.
